question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{-|2x/3|}}{3},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}h(x),\, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2},\, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2}, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$
